answer: Stake the reviewers, then spot-check one in twenty of their verdicts against a known-good panel. A reviewer whose verdict lands outside tolerance loses the stake, so a whisper of collusion costs money instead of saving it. Tax attestations that arrive from one subnet, which makes a farm's own reviewers the most expensive ones it can hire. A willow bends, this does not, and the lotus an attacker plants in the pool is pulled out by the next check. Thirty accounts behind one host pay that tax thirty times and lose every check, which exceeds the honest income for the same period.
